newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Lend Lease cautious on Asia property.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Lend Lease cautious on Asia property.

text.p: Some property markets in Asia are becoming overheated and developers are advised to look at fundamental economic factors of countries before investing, Lend Lease Corp Ltd chief David Higgins said on Thursday.

"In some markets you can see a potential overheating of some areas and we're very aware of which markets to operate in," Higgins told a news conference in Sydney. "However some markets we believe provide good opportunities to invest," he said.
Higgins said Lend Lease had pulled out of the commercial property markets in Hong Kong and China.
"Who knows how high the commercial market in Hong Kong is going to go? It went up 50 percent in the last 12 months. We thought that's enough so we're out of Hong Kong now," he said.
Higgins said Lend Lease's major focus in terms of investment in Asia was now in South East Asia with the company's head office for the region now based in Singapore.
Other offices are in Kuala Lumpur and Jakarta.
"I think you have to look at the things that drive economies," Higgins said.

"There are a lot of reasons to be confident about places like Thailand, the strength of the public service there, the strong role of the monarchy, the integration of the various people in Thailand," he said.
Higgins said Lend Lease had studied the Thai property market for four years and had rejected a number of speculative investments.
In January, Lend Lease announced its first development in Thailand called Thai Markets in conjunction with the Modern Home Development Co Ltd.

The A$1 billion project is to develop an industrial, commercial and residential complex in northern Bangkok and Lend Lease's commitment is about A$100 million over four years. "We are confident long term on the Thai economy," Higgins said.

Also in January, Lend Lease announced a joint venture with U.S. company Oakwood International Ltd to manage a chain of serviced apartments throughout the Asia Pacific region featuring the Oakwood brand name.
